title_vi: Event sourcing: lưu sự kiện thay vì trạng thái

claims.claim_vi: The source says event sourcing persists events instead of states with the event store as source of truth, and gives three examples: a newspaper keeping every article since 1851 as events denormalised into search nodes, a change-data-capture connector turning table changes into events pushed to Kafka, and microservices exchanging events (a shopping-cart service as producer, fraud, billing and email services as consumers).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Each entity has its own append-only eventstream; current state is derived by replaying the stream (rehydration); snapshots every N events are an optimisation, not a replacement; optimistic concurrency rejects an append when the stream changed since it was read.
claims.verified_by: Read from docs/patterns/event-sourcing.md of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center (main branch, fetched 2026-10-19).

claims.claim_vi: Drawbacks: eventual consistency of projections, immutability needs compensating events and event versioning (tolerant deserialization, versioning, upcasting), at-least-once delivery needs idempotent consumers, personal-data deletion conflicts with an append-only store (store data outside events or crypto-shredding), and a message broker like Kafka does not replace an event store.

Toy run: 100500 add/remove events over 50 items; replay from scratch applies 100500 events; from the snapshot at event 100000 (taken every 1000) it applies 500 and reaches the same state; two writers reading version 0 both append, the first succeeds and the second is rejected.
claims.verified_by: Run by the author on 2026-10-19 with a small Python program; counts only, no timing.

design_notes_vi: Một sơ đồ trình tự ba bên và một khung ghi chú kết quả thử.
source_deviations: The source gives three use cases; the lesson keeps them and adds rehydration, snapshots, optimistic concurrency and the known drawbacks from Microsoft's pattern page.
The lesson adds a counting experiment, which the source does not contain.
